title: Quiz: Variables Control Charts — Xbar-R and Xbar-S

questions.text: For an Xbar-R chart with subgroup size n=4, R̄ = 3.2 mm, and A₂ = 0.729, and x̄̄ = 50.0 mm — what is the UCL of the Xbar chart?
questions.explanation: UCL for the Xbar chart = x̄̄ + A₂ × R̄ = 50.0 + 0.729 × 3.2 = 52.33 mm. The constant A₂ depends on subgroup size n.

questions.text: Which chart in a control chart pair monitors process SPREAD (variability)?
options: Neither — control charts only monitor the mean
questions.explanation: The R chart (or S chart) monitors process spread/variability within subgroups. The Xbar chart monitors the process location (mean). Both are always used together.

questions.text: An Xbar chart that shows all points within control limits proves the process is producing conforming products.
questions.explanation: An in-control Xbar chart means the process location is statistically stable — not that products meet specification. Process capability (Cp, Cpk) determines whether the process meets specifications.

questions.text: According to the Western Electric rules, eight consecutive points on the same side of the centre line indicate:
options: A probable process shift — an out-of-control signal
An error in the control chart constants
The subgroup size is too large
questions.explanation: Eight consecutive points on the same side of the CL is a Western Electric run rule — it signals a probable process shift even if no single point exceeds the 3σ limits.

questions.text: The Xbar-S chart is preferred over Xbar-R when the subgroup size is greater than 10.
questions.explanation: For larger subgroups (n > 10), the within-subgroup standard deviation S is a more efficient estimator of process spread than the range R, so the Xbar-S chart is used.
